review_title: Surgical methods for first trimester termination of pregnancy
screening_criteria: Randomised controlled trials comparing different surgical methods for first trimester abortion were eligible.
gold_label_policy_description: dataset labels 1.0 and 0.5 count as INCLUDE; 0.0 counts as EXCLUDE

studies.study_title: Early complication after induced first‐trimaster abortion
studies.predicted_reason: This study reports a retrospective analysis of complications after 5,851 consecutive induced first-trimester abortions using bivariable analysis. There is no mention of randomisation or a comparison between different surgical methods. It appears to be an observational cohort study, not an RCT comparing surgical methods.

studies.study_title: Manual vacuum aspiration, a safe and effective alternative in early pregnancy termination
studies.predicted_reason: This is a randomised study of 200 women assigned to conventional vacuum aspiration (VA) or manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) for first-trimester termination (<56 days). It directly compares two different surgical methods in an RCT design, meeting the eligibility criteria.

studies.study_title: Induced termination of pregnancy before and after Roe v Wade. Trends in the mortality and morbidity of women
studies.predicted_reason: The study compares mortality and morbidity trends before and after the 1973 Roe v Wade decision. It is not a randomised controlled trial, nor does it compare different surgical methods for first-trimester abortion. It is a population-level temporal analysis.

Although this is a multicentre randomised trial, the comparison is between a prostaglandin vaginal suppository and placebo prior to vacuum aspiration. Both groups undergo the same surgical method (vacuum aspiration); the trial evaluates cervical preparation rather than comparing different surgical methods for termination.

studies.study_title: A comparison of D&C and vacuum aspiration for performing first trimester abortion
studies.predicted_reason: In this study 420 women were randomly assigned to dilatation and curettage (D&C) or vacuum aspiration (VA) for first-trimester abortion. It is an RCT explicitly comparing two different surgical methods, fitting the review objective and selection criteria.

studies.study_title: Acceptability of manual versus electric aspiration for first trimester abortion: a randomised trial
studies.predicted_reason: Eighty-four women seeking first-trimester abortion (<10 weeks) were randomised to manual or electric vacuum aspiration. This is an RCT comparing two distinct surgical aspiration methods, making it eligible.

studies.study_title: Similarities in women's perception and acceptability of manual vacuum aspiration and electric vacuum aspiration for first trimester abortion.
studies.predicted_reason: Women requesting first-trimester abortion were randomly assigned to manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) or electric vacuum aspiration (EVA). The abstract explicitly describes random allocation and compares two surgical methods, so it meets the eligibility criteria.

studies.study_title: Abortion by means of suction curettage compared to conventional metal curette
studies.predicted_reason: Forty-seven women underwent abortion by vacuum aspiration or classical dilatation and curettage. However, the abstract does not mention randomisation, and the wording suggests a non-randomised comparative or cohort design. Because the selection criteria require RCTs and there is no evidence of random allocation, this study is excluded at title/abstract screening.

studies.study_title: First trimester abortion by vacuum aspiration
studies.predicted_reason: This study randomly assigned 300 subjects to metal or flexible plastic cannulae for vacuum aspiration. While it is an RCT, it compares equipment (cannula types) within the same surgical method rather than comparing different surgical methods (e.g., D&C vs VA, or MVA vs VA). Therefore it does not meet the review objective.

studies.study_title: Comparison of pain and time of procedure with two first trimester abortion techniques performed by residents and faculty
studies.predicted_reason: One hundred and fourteen women undergoing first-trimester abortion were enrolled in a randomised trial comparing manual vacuum aspiration with electric vacuum curettage. This is an RCT comparing two surgical methods for first-trimester termination and is eligible.
